Citing the literature, the statement’s policy mix is consistent with rule-like behavior and effective lower-bound strategies, which offsets some of the negative public-health outlook. With inflation below target and labor-market slack, maintaining the funds rate at 0–0.25% and signaling average-inflation targeting aligns with Taylor-rule/New Keynesian guidance (Taylor; Clarida, Galí, and Gertler) and forecast-targeting principles (Svensson; Woodford) that help anchor expectations. Continued Treasury and MBS purchases support market functioning and the flow of credit through the credit channel (Bernanke, Gertler, Gilchrist), easing financial conditions. That said, substantial virus-related downside risks remain, and empirical DSGE evidence (e.g., Lubik and Schorfheide) suggests such shocks can dominate near-term dynamics. Netting policy support against health and macro risks, the tone is slightly negative but less so than a strongly risk-off reading.
